text_simplified: Children who enjoy warm and positive relationships with their teachers in kindergarten are more enthusiastic about learning, more confident in themselves, and achieve better results in the classroom. Likewise, sensitive and responsive relationships between parents and their child are linked to stronger cognitive skills and better social competence in school. Unfortunately, the poor quality of care in many childcare centers in the United States—due to high caregiver turnover and inadequate programs—does not support these benefits.
